source.title: GAMSAT Information Booklet 2026
source.note: Facts and short descriptive quotations from ACER's own published booklet, recorded to ground the move taxonomy. ACER's booklet is their copyright; nothing here is a test item, and no ACER question, passage or option is reproduced.

testWindows.note: New in 2026: the exam is split into two separate windows, not one sitting.
testWindows.first: Written Communication, remote proctored for all test takers
testWindows.second: Reasoning in Humanities and Social Sciences + Reasoning in Biological and Physical Sciences, at in-person test centres, approximately three weeks after the Written Communication window

sections.name: Reasoning in Humanities and Social Sciences

acerSkillFamilies.quote: recognition of explicit and implicit meanings through close reading of words and phrases as well as global interpretations of texts
interrelating, elaborating and extending concepts and ideas, and drawing conclusions
make discriminations and judgments in the realm of plausible reasoning

sections.name: Written Communication
sections.format: two writing tasks on a common theme

acerCriteria.gloss: the quality of what is said — what is made of and developed from the task, and the kinds of thoughts offered
the quality of the structure developed and language used — the shape and form of the piece

sections.note: ACER states pre-prepared and memorised responses score poorly and may be flagged as plagiarised. Nothing in this project should encourage a pre-written essay.

sections.name: Reasoning in Biological and Physical Sciences
sections.assumedKnowledge: first year of university studies in biology and chemistry, and A-level/Leaving Certificate/Year 12 in physics
sections.assumedKnowledgeCaveat: The test however, focuses primarily on problem solving and on the use of the prerequisite knowledge.
acerSkills: translate knowledge from one form to another
formulate and apply hypotheses and make generalisations
follow and evaluate a line of reasoning
categorise and select information relevant to problems
generate and apply strategies to solve problems

scoring.formula: (1 x Humanities & Social Sciences + 1 x Written Communication + 2 x Biological & Physical Sciences) / 4
scoring.implication: Section III is double-weighted and is therefore 50% of the overall score on its own — the single highest-leverage section to target.

licence.note: This structured record is our own compilation. The quoted phrases are short factual descriptors attributed to ACER.

scopeOfAuthority.trustFor: Structure: question counts, timings, section weighting, discipline proportions, test-window arrangement.
scopeOfAuthority.doNotTrustFor: What the exam actually rewards. The skill descriptors here are the construct as DECLARED, and are too generic to discriminate. ACER free practice material is also widely reported as easier than and unrepresentative of the live exam, so neither the booklet nor the free samples should be treated as ground truth for difficulty or for which reasoning moves carry marks.
